record.paper_title: Open problems in nuclear structure near drip lines
record.context_brief: Energy density functional for drip lines
record.original_question: How should the nuclear energy density functional be extended so that it can make reliable predictions at the drip lines? This includes explaining the Wigner energy in nuclei with equal neutron and proton numbers near the proton drip line, determining whether isoscalar T = 0 pairing is responsible for that extra binding, and constructing a functional that remains valid despite incomplete knowledge of low-density clustering and high-density many-body interactions, so that empirical data near the drip lines can properly constrain the functional form.

evidence.quote: Despite of recent efforts to improve the energy density functional, it is still far from solid prediction of the drip lines (see Sec. 1).

A major problem at the proton drip line is related to the Wigner energy in N = Z nuclei. It cannot be explained by conventional density functionals and its extension is necessary. There are some arguments that the isoscalar (T = 0) pairing might be responsible for the Wigner energy [32, 33], but it is not conclusive yet.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Construct an extension of the nuclear energy density functional (EDF) framework that yields reliable predictions of the proton and neutron drip lines across the nuclear chart. Specifically:

1. Within an EDF formalism for the nuclear ground-state energy E[ρ_n, ρ_p, τ_n, τ_p, J_n, J_p, …] (and associated pairing tensors κ), produce a functional form whose minimization reproduces empirical binding energies, separation energies, and other available data near both drip lines, while remaining well-behaved in regimes where (a) low-density α-like clustering is expected to be important and (b) high-density many-body correlations are not fully known.

2. Account quantitatively for the Wigner energy: the additional binding observed in nuclei with equal neutron and proton numbers (N = Z), which conventional Skyrme- or Gogny-type EDFs (with only isovector T = 1 pairing) fail to reproduce. Determine whether the inclusion of isoscalar (T = 0) neutron–proton pairing — i.e., a pair condensate with total isospin T = 0, S = 1 — in the EDF is sufficient to explain this extra binding, or whether additional ingredients (e.g., quartet correlations, beyond-mean-field projection on isospin) are required.

3. Demonstrate that, with this extended functional, empirical data near the drip lines can in fact constrain the functional parameters in a stable way, so that extrapolation to nuclei beyond present experimental reach yields predictions with controlled uncertainties.

Provide explicit forms of the functional, the pairing channels (T = 0 and T = 1), and a fitting protocol, and verify the construction on N = Z nuclei near the proton drip line.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (through 2024–2026) confirms that an EDF that reliably predicts drip lines and fully accounts for the Wigner energy in N = Z nuclei is still being actively pursued. Studies using quark–meson-coupling EDFs combined with quartet condensation, generator-coordinate methods with proton–neutron pairing fluctuations, and analyses of isovector vs. isoscalar pairing indicate that T = 0 isoscalar p–n pairing is the leading candidate for explaining the Wigner energy, but the question is not conclusively settled and a universally predictive functional at the drip lines has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Proton-Neutron Pairing in N=Z Nuclei within the Quark-Meson-Coupling Energy Density Functional
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the impact of isovector and isoscalar proton-neutron pairing correlations using QMC EDF combined with quartet condensation model.
status_evidence.claim: Construction of EDFs that incorporate T=0 p-n pairing for N=Z nuclei is still an active research topic.

status_evidence.title: Generator Coordinate Method with Proton–Neutron Pairing Fluctuations and Magnetic Properties of N = Z Odd–Odd Nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) treatment of T=0 and T=1 p-n pairing fluctuations in N=Z nuclei via GCM beyond mean field.
status_evidence.claim: The role of T=0 pairing in N=Z nuclei is still being investigated, indicating the problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Relation between Wigner energy and proton-neutron pairing
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the link between the Wigner energy and proton-neutron pairing.
status_evidence.claim: The Wigner energy is widely associated with p-n pairing but a definitive EDF resolution remains lacking.

status_evidence.title: Application of Nuclear Density Functional Theory to Exotic Nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Dissertation on extending nuclear DFT to exotic nuclei near drip lines.
status_evidence.claim: Extending EDFs for reliable drip-line predictions is still an open research direction.
